rationale.conceptual: The solver blends Q-tensor dynamics with a D3Q19 lattice Boltzmann method, requiring knowledge of liquid crystal physics and numerical methods. While the model is documented, implementing the coupled equations correctly demands careful attention to discretization, boundary conditions, and parameter scaling; it is not a simple off-the-shelf library call but also not a new algorithm.
rationale.execution: The workflow consists of only three main steps (implement solver, run two simulations, compute averages) with no complex orchestration, external tooling, or data acquisition. The only dependency is having the solver ready before the production runs, making it a straightforward multi-step pipeline.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires implementing a hybrid finite-difference/lattice-Boltzmann solver for the Beris-Edwards model of active nematodynamics on a 201³ periodic grid, running two simulations, and extracting time-averaged defect density and RMS velocity. The method is an established but non-trivial continuum simulation requiring careful implementation of the governing equations, and the pipeline consists of a few straightforward sequential steps. Resource needs are moderate, with CPU-only LBM computations and about 3-4 GB RAM.

compute_estimate.reasoning: A 3D LBM simulation on a 201³ grid with Q-tensor, velocity, and distribution function arrays requires roughly 3–4 GB of RAM per run; no external dataset is needed, and the computation is CPU-bound.
